errors.text: The proposed optimum of 850–900 °C is opposite to the target result, in which SPS at 1000 °C gives the best density, hardness, oxidation resistance, and corrosion resistance.
The hypothesis omits the MgAlTiVFeCo composition, its ball-milled BCC starting phase, and the use of spark plasma sintering.

It incorrectly treats 1000 °C as a poor-volatility/segregation baseline and moves the volatility boundary to above 950 °C, whereas the supported boundary permits processing up to 1000 °C and only excludes temperatures above it.
The proposed FCC/B2 stabilization and suppression of oxides conflict with the target mediator: uniformly distributed AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3 barrier phases formed at the high-temperature optimum.

The claimed effects of oxygen on alpha-HCP stabilization and the proposed Laves/Heusler transformations are extrapolated from materially different alloy systems without direct support for the MgAlTiVFeCo alloy.
The experiment omits the critical 1000 °C sample, the 900 °C air-oxidation condition, and electrochemical corrosion testing in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
